facts.statement: Vegavis lived in Antarctica during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Vegavis is a genus of extinct avian dinosaur that lived in Antarctica during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The type species Vegavis iaai was named in 2005 based on fossils from the López de Bertodano Formation.
facts.quote: The type species is Vegavis iaai, named in 2005 based on fossils from the López de Bertodano Formation.

facts.statement: Two additional species, Vegavis geitononesos and Vegavis notopothousa, were named in 2026 based on material from the López de Bertodano Formation.
facts.quote: Two additional species, Vegavis geitononesos and Vegavis notopothousa, were named in 2026 based on additional material from the same formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Vegavis is held by the Museo de La Plata in Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype is held by the Museo de La Plata, Argentina.

facts.statement: Researchers used CT scans to study the holotype's bone structure without damaging the fossil.
facts.quote: CT scans were utilized to gain a clearer picture of the bone structure without running danger of damaging or destroying the fossil.

facts.statement: The syrinx of Vegavis had an asymmetrical third segment and large soft-tissue resonating structures, suggesting it could produce honks like ducks and geese.
facts.quote: The syrinx has an asymmetrical third segment, suggesting that Vegavis had two sources of sound in the neck and along with large soft-tissue resonating structures.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skull discovered in 2011 was officially described in 2025 and assigned to Vegavis.
facts.quote: A nearly complete skull specimen (AMNH FARB 30899) discovered by Eric M. Roberts in 2011 from the Sandwich Bluff Member of the López de Bertodano Formation on Vega Island was officially described in 2025.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists debate whether Vegavis belongs to Anseriformes or is a stem-group bird with an unresolved position at the base of Neognathae.
facts.quote: However, some paleontologists questioned its affinities to Anseriformes or Galloanserae, with some classifying it as a stem-group bird within Ornithurae, a crown group bird outside Galloanserae, a sister taxon of the Neornithes or at the base of Neognathae with an unresolved position.

facts.statement: Vegavis had a high metabolism that allowed it to survive at high latitudes in Antarctica.
facts.quote: Vegavis was a bird with a high metabolism, which allowed it to live at high latitudes in Antarctica.

facts.statement: Vegavis exhibited osteosclerosis, a condition possibly related to variations in diving behavior.
facts.quote: It also shows a degree of osteosclerosis, a condition shared with Polarornis. This different degrees of osteosclerosis could be related to variations in diving behaviour.

facts.statement: The type locality for V. geitononesos dates to the uppermost Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The upper Molluscan Allomember (unit klb 9) of the Lopez de Bertodano Formation on Seymour (Marambio) Island, the type locality of V. geitononesos, is dated to the uppermost Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Vegavis iaai is classified in the order Anseriformes.
Vegavis iaai is classified in the family Vegaviidae.
Vegavis iaai lived in Antarctica during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) about 65 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vegavis iaai es una especie extinta de aves anseriformes de la familia Vegaviidae y único miembro conocido del género Vegavis, que vivió durante el Cretácico Superior (estadio Maastrichtiense) de la Antártida, hace unos 65 millones de años.

facts.statement: The discovery of Vegavis iaai demonstrates that major groups of living birds had already diversified by the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de la especie tipo, Vegavis iaai, demuestra que los mayores grupos de aves actualmente vivientes se habían ya diversificado en el Cretácico.

facts.statement: The specimen was found in 1992 but described as a new species in 2005 due to its delicate nature embedded in a concretion.
facts.quote: El espécimen, catalogado como MLP 93-I-3-1, fue encontrado en depósitos del Cabo Lamb de la Isla Vega, Antártica, en 1992, pero solo fue descrito como una nueva especie en 2005 porque consiste de restos muy delicados de un ave embebida en una concreción, la cual debía ser preparada meticulosamente para su estudio.

facts.statement: The genus Vegavis lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
